lessons.title: Audit XR demonstrations as training data
lessons.summary: Trace the official episode writer and define an acceptance contract for demonstrations. Validate timestamps, labels, assets, and recording completion.
objectives: Inspect actual recorded schema
Detect missing provenance and incomplete assets
Split demonstrations without episode leakage
prerequisites: The preceding lesson in this course, where present
An isolated Linux development environment; no robot connection required

sections.heading: A recording file is not automatically a dataset
sections.body: The official XR project can record teleoperation episodes, but the actual writer deserves inspection before data is used for learning. The pinned implementation starts with placeholder task text and empty joint-name metadata unless the application supplies meaningful values. Its items contain indices and modality fields; an item index alone does not establish capture time or synchronization. Audit how the caller supplies states, actions, camera frames and optional tactile data. Replace default descriptive text with the actual task definition and preserve the robot, hand, calibration and source revisions. A dataset should describe what happened, with what configuration, rather than inherit convenient example metadata.

sections.heading: Acquisition time and write time are different
sections.body: Camera exposure, joint-state reception, operator target generation and disk writing occur at different times. A writer that processes queued items later cannot use its write-time log as proof that the sensor samples were synchronized. Record capture or receive timestamps and their clock domains upstream. Define an alignment tolerance suitable for the experiment, then measure how many items violate it. The pinned writer uses a background queue and finalizes the JSON structure when an episode is saved. Verify finalization and asset existence before accepting the episode. A process stopping after enqueueing data may leave an incomplete artifact even though the user pressed the record key.

sections.heading: Preserve modality semantics and failure evidence
sections.body: The writer stores depth images using an image-writing path with a JPEG filename in the examined implementation. Before treating those files as metric depth, inspect the caller’s data type, encoding, scale and any preprocessing. A visualization image is not automatically lossless metric depth. The same principle applies to actions: a desired target, retargeted command and measured achieved pose are different labels. Keep their identities separate. Validate every referenced asset, image dimensions, frame count, joint-name order and missing-modality policy. Retain failed attempts with an outcome label when they are useful; do not silently erase them while later claiming the data represent the full operating distribution.

sections.heading: Split by episodes and conditions
sections.body: Randomly assigning adjacent frames from one demonstration to training and evaluation creates leakage because the frames are highly correlated. Split at least by complete episode, and consider separating object instances, sessions, operators or environments according to the intended generalization claim. A worked example is ten episodes of the same cup in one scene: a held-out frame split tests very little beyond interpolation in that scene. A held-out session or object condition asks a stronger question. Record the split rule and hashes of accepted episodes. The lab produces a dataset audit, not a trained model; its value is preventing broken timing, placeholder labels and leakage from being mistaken for algorithmic progress.

lessons.title: Reconstruct the G1 policy observation and action contract
lessons.summary: Read an actual RL configuration and exported deployment parameters. Verify ordering, history, scaling, offsets, and joint permutation before inference.
objectives: Calculate the policy observation dimension
Validate a joint permutation
Explain action scaling and multirate execution
prerequisites: The preceding lesson in this course, where present
An isolated Linux development environment; no robot connection required

sections.heading: A model tensor needs a semantic map
sections.body: The pinned G1 velocity environment lists policy observations in a defined order: angular velocity, projected gravity, velocity command, relative joint position, relative joint velocity and previous action. For the 29-joint configuration, their single-step dimensions are three, three, three, twenty-nine, twenty-nine and twenty-nine, totaling ninety-six. The configuration uses a history length of five, producing a 480-value concatenated history under that contract. The exact memory ordering of history and terms must still be verified in the observation implementation and export path; a correct total dimension does not prove correct ordering. Build a table of every slice, scale, frame and source rather than passing an anonymous 480-element array to a model.

sections.heading: Training observations and privileged information differ
sections.body: The environment defines policy and critic observation groups separately. The critic can receive information used during training that is not part of the deployed policy input. Do not copy every available simulator quantity into the runtime policy vector because it appears useful. Conversely, omitting required history or using absolute positions where relative positions are expected changes the input distribution. Test preprocessing using synthetic states with distinctive values. Record the zero reference and scaling for every term, including velocity scales and projected-gravity frame. A tensor can have the expected shape and dtype while being semantically wrong in every element. That is why schema and numerical fixture tests belong beside the exported model.

sections.heading: Actions need scaling, offsets and a verified permutation
sections.body: The reviewed deployment parameters include a joint index map, action scale and default offset. A network output is not automatically a direct joint angle or torque. In this policy contract, joint-position actions are scaled and offset before the hardware-facing mapping is applied. Validate the map as a permutation of the expected joint indices and verify its direction with named fixtures; an inverse permutation can pass a simple uniqueness test yet still be used incorrectly. Keep the model, parameter file and robot map as one release unit. Swapping a newer parameter file beneath an older model can change behavior without changing the model’s filename or tensor dimensions.
sections.code:
# Exact permutation copied as data from the pinned deployment YAML.
policy_to_device = [0,6,12,1,7,13,2,8,14,3,9,15,22,4,10,16,23,5,11,
                    17,24,18,25,19,26,20,27,21,28]
assert sorted(policy_to_device) == list(range(29))
# This fixture assumes that direction; confirm against runtime code.
policy_values = [1000+i for i in range(29)]
device_values = [None]*29
for policy_index, device_index in enumerate(policy_to_device):
    device_values[device_index] = policy_values[policy_index]
round_trip = [device_values[i] for i in policy_to_device]
assert round_trip == policy_values
assert device_values[6] == 1001
terms = [3,3,3,29,29,29]
assert sum(terms) == 96
assert sum(terms)*5 == 480
print({"step_values": 96, "history_values": 480, "policy_hz": 1/(0.005*4)})
sections.callout: Course-authored offline exercise. It does not publish robot commands or establish hardware acceptance.

sections.heading: Policy and physics rates are distinct
sections.body: The training configuration uses a five-millisecond physics step with decimation four, giving a twenty-millisecond policy step. The deployment parameters also state a twenty-millisecond step. This is fifty policy decisions per second, not the same claim as a two-millisecond low-level command loop. A lower-level loop may hold or interpolate policy outputs under a defined control contract. Inspect that behavior instead of assuming the neural network runs at every motor update. In the lab, calculate the rates, build the observation vector from fixtures, and test action scaling and permutation without running a robot. The outcome is a reproducible inference contract with explicit ordering and timing assumptions.

lessons.title: Evaluate sim-to-sim transfer and domain randomization
lessons.summary: Design a transfer test that targets model mismatch rather than a selected demo. Compare physics assumptions, observations, delays, and failure distributions.
objectives: Distinguish randomization from coverage
Design controlled cross-simulator comparisons
Report failures and observation mismatches
prerequisites: The preceding lesson in this course, where present
An isolated Linux development environment; no robot connection required

sections.heading: Transfer tests are about mismatched assumptions
sections.body: The official RL workflow recommends testing a trained strategy in MuJoCo before physical deployment. Moving between simulators can expose differences in contact, actuator models, integration, joint ordering and observation construction. It is not a ritual that guarantees physical success. Start with a contract comparison: robot geometry and mass, joint limits, default pose, action scale, control period, estimator inputs and termination conditions. If those differ unintentionally, fix the contract before interpreting a policy failure as a learning problem. Keep intentional differences as named experimental variables. Otherwise a successful video may simply reflect easier dynamics, privileged observations or a different task rather than robust transfer.

sections.heading: Randomization must match a hypothesis
sections.body: The reviewed environment randomizes selected physical properties and reset conditions and includes periodic perturbations. These choices expand the training distribution, but they do not cover every real-world uncertainty. More randomness is not automatically better: unrealistic combinations can make the task impossible or encourage behavior irrelevant to the intended deployment. State which uncertainty each randomized parameter represents and where its range came from. For course experiments, label ranges as illustrative when they are not measured. Evaluate both inside and outside the training ranges, with separate reporting. A single average across all conditions can hide a sharp failure boundary near a particular friction, delay or mass combination.

sections.heading: Use controlled sweeps and held-out seeds
sections.body: Choose a small baseline configuration, then vary one factor at a time before testing combinations. For example, compare observation delay, mass perturbation and contact-friction assumptions while keeping the initial condition and policy fixed. Record seeds so paired comparisons are possible. Measure task error, falls or termination, joint-limit activity, modeled effort, latency and recovery behavior as appropriate. Preserve the full trial distribution. Do not discard a failed rollout because the simulator looked awkward; classify whether it was a model import error, contract mismatch or genuine policy failure. These categories lead to different next steps and prevent retraining from becoming the default response to every problem.

sections.heading: Plan the acceptance boundary explicitly
sections.body: A transfer report should state which simulators and versions were used, which contract elements matched, which parameters varied, and what criterion was set before the evaluation. Keep simulation domains and loopback isolation consistent on every endpoint, even when upstream deployment instructions use a hardware-default domain. The lab can be completed with a small policy fixture if the full training stack is unavailable, but that limitation must be stated; do not imply a neural policy was trained when only preprocessing was tested. Successful sim-to-sim results justify the next review stage. They do not remove the need for exact firmware, actuator, support-fixture and supervised physical prerequisites before hardware experiments.

questions.prompt: Does randomizing more parameters guarantee robust transfer?
choices: Yes, if every physical parameter is randomized independently
Yes
Yes, if the randomized training set is large enough regardless of parameter ranges
No; ranges and combinations must reflect a stated uncertainty hypothesis
questions.explanation: Randomization provides coverage of a chosen distribution, not all possible real-world behavior.

questions.prompt: Why keep paired seeds in baseline and perturbed trials?
choices: They eliminate all uncertainty
They make the simulated physics identical across different engines
They replace the need for held-out conditions and multiple trials
They reduce uncontrolled variation when attributing changes to the tested factor
questions.explanation: Paired conditions support a cleaner comparison while preserving the need for multiple trials and honest limits.

lessons.title: Capstone: ship a reproducible robot research release
lessons.summary: Package code, models, policies, datasets, and operational evidence as one reviewable system. Define rollback and recovery without claiming untested hardware readiness.
objectives: Create a complete release manifest
Link requirements to evidence
Design failure recovery and version rollback
prerequisites: The preceding lesson in this course, where present
An isolated Linux development environment; no robot connection required

sections.heading: Version the whole behavior-producing system
sections.body: A robot release includes more than application source. Its behavior depends on firmware, SDK, middleware, model files, calibration, joint maps, policy weights, preprocessing, task configuration and sometimes the dataset used to train it. Capture exact revisions or hashes and record which components were observed on hardware versus selected for simulation. The Unitree model distribution has moved from a deprecated GitHub repository to a newer source, which illustrates why a URL alone is not enough. Archive or hash the actual permitted artifacts used in your experiment. A release manifest should make an accidental combination of old weights and new action offsets immediately visible.
sections.code:
# Usage: python manifest.py file1 file2 ...
import hashlib, json, pathlib, sys
records = []
for name in sys.argv[1:]:
    path = pathlib.Path(name)
    digest = hashlib.sha256()
    with path.open("rb") as handle:
        for chunk in iter(lambda: handle.read(1024*1024), b""):
            digest.update(chunk)
    records.append({"path": str(path), "bytes": path.stat().st_size,
                    "sha256": digest.hexdigest()})
print(json.dumps(records, indent=2))
sections.callout: Course-authored offline exercise. It does not publish robot commands or establish hardware acceptance.

sections.heading: Build a requirement-to-evidence map
sections.body: Each important requirement should point to a test and its result. Configuration matching can point to a joint-map fixture; stale-input inhibition to a fault test; episode completeness to a dataset audit; sim-to-sim behavior to a trial report. Keep evidence claims bounded. A passing synthetic stale-input test proves the application’s tested response, not the physical robot’s emergency stop behavior. A source review can establish that an example creates a publisher, but it cannot establish achieved network latency. This map helps reviewers separate code facts, measured behavior and remaining assumptions. It also prevents a large collection of screenshots from being mistaken for comprehensive validation.

sections.heading: Recovery is part of the release, not an afterthought
sections.body: Document what the application does after lost telemetry, rejected ownership handoff, invalid model input, interrupted recording or process restart. Recovery should re-establish necessary state and configuration rather than replay old commands. A rollback plan identifies a previously validated software package and compatible configuration; it should not casually downgrade firmware or mix arbitrary library versions. Keep physical recovery steps delegated to the current vendor manual and competent local supervision. The software runbook can still specify logs to preserve, processes to stop, and evidence required before a new session. Practice those paths with fake transport and simulation so the first failure is not the first time the team has considered recovery.

sections.heading: Make the final review candid and useful
sections.body: The capstone review has four decisions: what was built, what was tested, what failed, and what remains outside the evidence. Include a small reproducibility procedure another engineer can run from a clean workspace. Report actual test counts and environments, not invented certification or deployment claims. If hardware was never connected, say so clearly. If a vendor protocol was unavailable, identify the exact blocked integration and retain the completed offline work. A course can take a learner toward expert practice by demanding this precision; expertise is not awarded merely for reaching the final page. The release succeeds when its behavior and limitations are inspectable enough for someone else to challenge, reproduce and improve.
